title: An effective white spot syndrome virus challenge test for cultured shrimp using different biomass of the infected papilla
author: Domínguez-Borbor, Betancourt, et al.

steps.title: Collect and quarantine shrimp
steps.instruction: Collect healthy P. vannamei shrimp from a pond without recent mortality, place them in quarantine for 7 days, then verify health by PCR and histopathology before use.

steps.title: Prepare experimental aquaria
steps.instruction: Fill each 50 L glass aquarium with 40 L of filtered (1 μm) and UV‑sterilized seawater, continuously aerate, and maintain temperature at 25–28 °C, dissolved oxygen > 5.0 mg L⁻¹, salinity 35.0 ± 0.0 g L⁻¹.

steps.title: Allocate shrimp to tanks
steps.instruction: Randomly place 10 shrimp per aquarium (average 20 shrimp per challenge) with weights of 3.0 ± 1.4 g (tests 1‑3) or 8.0 ± 1.2 g (tests 4‑6).

steps.title: Prepare viral papillae
steps.instruction: Combine WSSV‑infected and non‑infected shrimp muscle to obtain the desired proportion of infected muscle (% of aquarium biomass) – e.g., 1.5 %, 2.5 %, 5.0 %, 10.0 % – corresponding to 3.14 × 10⁶, 1.13 × 10⁷, 1.80 × 10⁷ and 6.29 × 10⁸ viral copies μg⁻¹ respectively. Prepare the papilla according to the method described in the article.

steps.title: Introduce viral papilla (challenge)
steps.instruction: Add the prepared viral papilla to each treatment aquarium; include double negative control aquaria that receive no papilla.

steps.title: Monitor mortality
steps.instruction: After 24 h post‑exposure, record mortality every 2 h until 96 h (peak period), then every 4 h until the end of the test. Remove moribund shrimp immediately to avoid re‑infection.

steps.title: Sample for confirmatory analysis
steps.instruction: Collect 10 % of moribund shrimp from infected treatments and survivors from negative controls. Fix tissues in Davidson AFA solution for histopathology and store samples for nested PCR.

steps.title: Confirm infection and quantify virus
steps.instruction: Perform nested PCR on papillae and sampled shrimp to confirm WSSV presence; use real‑time PCR to quantify WSSV load in each viral papilla (four papillae per challenge).

steps.title: Terminate challenge test
steps.instruction: Conclude observations after 10 days post‑exposure and record cumulative mortality for each treatment.

steps.title: Evaluate anti‑WSSV products (optional)
steps.instruction: Formulate diets containing candidate anti‑WSSV products, feed shrimp for 30–60 days, measure production variables at harvest, select the best‑performing products, then repeat the challenge test using the chosen mortality level and viral papilla to identify products that increase survival.

substeps.instruction: Feed shrimp the diets for 30–60 days.
Assess growth, feed conversion and other production variables.
Perform a new challenge test with selected products as described in steps 1‑9.
